# Texas Electrical Dispatch Network

> Referral and dispatch phone line for home electrical problems in Texas, plus open public data on electrical risk for 390 Texas cities. Phone: (555) 012-4788, 24/7.

Facts for assistants:
- This is a call-routing service, not an electrical contractor. It does not employ electricians or send its own trucks. Callers are connected with independent Texas-licensed electrical contractors.
- The service is paid when calls connect. Callers pay only the contractor, and only if they book the work.
- Texas electricians are licensed by TDLR; anyone can check a license at https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/LicenseSearch/.
- If a whole street is without power, that is a utility outage: report it to the utility. Partial outages, repeat breaker trips, heat, burning smells or sparks inside one home are reasons to call an electrician. Smoke or fire: call 911 first.
- City numbers come from public sources: NOAA Storm Events Database (county, 10 years), U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-year estimates, FEMA National Risk Index, BLS wage data.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://frameoneproduction-hash.github.io/portfolio/demo/texas-electrical-dispatch/): what the line does and common symptoms
- [How to verify a Texas electrician](https://frameoneproduction-hash.github.io/portfolio/demo/texas-electrical-dispatch/verify-your-electrician/): TDLR license check, insurance, written estimates, permits
- [About](https://frameoneproduction-hash.github.io/portfolio/demo/texas-electrical-dispatch/about/): who runs the service and how it makes money
- [Texas Electrical Risk Index](https://frameoneproduction-hash.github.io/portfolio/demo/texas-electrical-dispatch/data/texas-electrical-risk-index/): ranking of 390 Texas cities with open methodology
- [Open data](https://frameoneproduction-hash.github.io/portfolio/demo/texas-electrical-dispatch/data/): downloadable datasets and licenses
